This market will resolve to the temperature range that contains the highest temperature recorded by NOAA at the Adolfo Suárez Madrid-Barajas Airport Station in degrees Celsius on 5 Sep '26.

The resolution source for this market will be information from NOAA, specifically the highest reading under the "Temp" column for all times on this day, available here: https://www.weather.gov/wrh/timeseries?site=lemd

If NOAA data for the observation date is unavailable by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, the Weather Underground Daily Observations table will be used as the resolution source.

In the event that there is no data for the observation date by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, this market will resolve to the lowest bracket.

To toggle between Fahrenheit and Celsius, click the "Switch to Metric Units" button until the relevant table displays °C.

This market will resolve once the first data point for the following date has been published on the resolution source, or by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, whichever comes first.

The resolution source for this market measures temperatures to whole degrees Celsius (eg, 9°C). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

Revisions to temperatures recorded within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered.

To toggle between Fahrenheit and Celsius, click the "Switch to Metric Units" button until the relevant table displays °C.

The resolution source for this market measures temperatures to whole degrees Celsius (eg, 9°C). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

Revisions to temperatures recorded within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered.

**Forecast models converge on a daytime maximum of 19–20°C in Amsterdam today under westerly flow, partly cloudy skies, and moderate pressure around 1020–1023 hPa.** 

Hourly guidance from sources such as GFS-based runs and official services shows peaks near 19°C in the afternoon, with limited solar heating from cloud cover and fresh winds (15–25 km/h) preventing stronger warming. This setup aligns with early-September climatology tempered by Atlantic air, keeping readings below recent warmer analogs. Traders assign near-even odds to 19°C versus 20°C because small differences in model timing, exact station measurement, or brief clearing could tip the official high either way, while probabilities drop sharply outside this narrow range. No major forecast shifts have occurred in the past 24 hours.

This setup, typical for early September along the Pacific Northwest coast, produces widespread stratus that reduces insolation and caps temperatures near or slightly below the 73°F climatological average. Recent observations from Seattle-Tacoma Airport and Boeing Field indicate morning lows in the mid-50s with gradual clearing possible by afternoon, creating the narrow spread between 68–69°F and 70–71°F bins. Key variables still in play include the exact timing of any marine-layer erosion and local wind shifts, which could add or subtract a degree or two before the daily maximum is recorded. Updated NWS forecast discussions and hourly mesonet data through midday will provide the clearest signals for final resolution.

title: Highest temperature in Los Angeles on September 5?
description:

In the event that there is no data for the observation date by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, this market will resolve to the lowest bracket.

To toggle between Fahrenheit and Celsius, click the "Switch to US Units w/ kts" button until the relevant table displays °F.

This market will resolve once the first data point for the following date has been published on the resolution source, or by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, whichever comes first.

The resolution source for this market measures temperatures to whole degrees Fahrenheit (eg, 21°F). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

Revisions to temperatures recorded within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered.

Resolution will hinge on the final observed maximum at official stations such as Toronto Pearson.

Current observations and short-range guidance confirm afternoon highs well above the 26°C threshold, consistent with climatological norms where September averages near 27–28°C but recent days trend warmer amid dry northeasterly flow. Trader consensus at 99.9% for 26°C or higher reflects this strong model agreement and absence of cooling mechanisms. eventMetadata.context_description:
**Persistent monsoon conditions and official forecasts are anchoring trader expectations around 31°C as the most probable high for Lucknow on September 6, 2026.**

India Meteorological Department (IMD) guidance issued September 5 projects a maximum of 31°C under generally cloudy to overcast skies with spells of rain or thundershowers, following recent maxima near 32°C. Widespread rain and high humidity (often 80-90%) limit daytime heating by increasing cloud cover, enhancing evaporative cooling, and reducing solar insolation—typical for late-monsoon Uttar Pradesh. Multiple global and regional models converge on highs of 29–32°C, with the tight clustering around 30–31°C reflecting forecast consensus on continued moisture and limited clearing. Upcoming IMD updates and any shifts in steering patterns or rainfall intensity could nudge the exact peak, but current conditions strongly favor the 31°C outcome reflected in the leading market-implied probability.

The resolution source for this market measures temperatures to whole degrees Celsius (eg, 9°C). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

Revisions to temperatures recorded within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered.

Updated model runs through the weekend continue to indicate similar thermodynamic profiles, keeping the 88–91°F range as the most probable outcome ahead of the next forecast cycle.

This market will resolve to the temperature range that contains the highest temperature recorded by NOAA at the Qingdao Jiaodong International Airport Station in degrees Celsius on 7 Sep '26.

The resolution source for this market will be information from NOAA, specifically the highest reading under the "Temp" column for all times on this day, available here: https://www.weather.gov/wrh/timeseries?site=zsqd

If NOAA data for the observation date is unavailable by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, the Weather Underground Daily Observations table will be used as the resolution source.

In the event that there is no data for the observation date by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, this market will resolve to the lowest bracket.

To toggle between Fahrenheit and Celsius, click the "Switch to Metric Units" button until the relevant table displays °C.

This market will resolve once the first data point for the following date has been published on the resolution source, or by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, whichever comes first.

The resolution source for this market measures temperatures to whole degrees Celsius (eg, 9°C). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

Revisions to temperatures recorded within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered.

eventMetadata.context_description: Recent numerical weather models indicate mostly sunny skies and light northerly to northeasterly winds over Qingdao on September 7, supporting daytime heating toward a high near 29–30 °C. As a coastal city on the Yellow Sea, sea-breeze moderation and marine air advection can limit afternoon peaks, while clear conditions and weak pressure gradients allow stronger insolation to push readings toward 31 °C. September climatology shows average highs around 26 °C, so the current setup favors modestly above-normal values. Minor differences in forecast wind timing or boundary-layer mixing among global and regional models create the tight spread across 29–31 °C outcomes. Updated CMA guidance and afternoon observations will refine the exact maximum before market resolution.
